The Abia State Police Command has explained its involvement in the disappearance of a nursing graduate, Fortunate Chiamaka Aku, after her father, Phillip Aku, appealed to the state governor, Alex Otti, and the new Commissioner of Police, Sylvester Adaji, to intervene and establish the whereabouts of his daughter. Aku alleged that his only daughter, a nursing graduate of Abia State University, Uturu, who is currently undergoing a one-year internship at the Abia Specialist Hospital, Umuahia, left home on Monday, November 23, for afternoon duty but reportedly ended up in an unknown location after she was allegedly hypnotised by criminals. He said the family became alarmed when Chiamaka failed to return home after her shift, adding that she was later found in a disoriented state around Umuikaa, Isiala Ngwa South Local Government Area, by a Good Samaritan. According to him, the Good Samaritan took Chiamaka to a nearby police station and recorded a video of her in an apparent state of confusion and exhaustion in an effort to locate her family. The video was subsequently circulated on Facebook, prompting Aku to rush to the police station after learning that his daughter had been found. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources However, he said he was shocked to discover that Chiamaka was no longer at the station when he arrived. Aku said the police officers confirmed that his daughter had been brought to the station the previous day and recognised her from the video, but could not account for her whereabouts. “They said this is the girl that was with them yesterday. She was here. I thought maybe they had kept her somewhere and would bring her out. Unfortunately, it was not like that,” he said. The father alleged that the officers told him they had released his daughter because the station lacked the facilities to keep her and they did not want to get into trouble. New Abia CP seeks public cooperation to tackle crime 2027: Cubana chief priest endorses Otti, LP Reps candidate Four schools benefit from free exercise books He expressed concern that a woman who was reportedly unable to communicate properly, visibly exhausted and in need of assistance could allegedly be released without efforts to establish her identity, locate her family or ensure her safety. Aku further alleged that when the officers offered to assist him in searching the surrounding area, they asked him to provide money for fuel for their vehicle. He appealed to the police authorities, Governor Otti, other security agencies and members of the public to urgently assist in finding his daughter. However, the Police Public Relations Officer in the state, DSP Maureen Chinaka, said the police did not have Chiamaka in their custody. Chinaka explained that a woman believed to be of unsound mind had been brought to the police division and that the officer on duty, after making inquiries, advised that she be taken to an appropriate facility for treatment because the station lacked the necessary facilities to care for her. “A person of unsound mind was brought to the police division. The officer on guard, after enquiry, asked that the lady be taken to the right place for treatment because the police station has no facilities for such people,” she said. According to the PPRO, the woman left the station with the person who brought her there. “The lady even followed the person that brought her to the station as he was leaving,” she added. Chinaka assured that the police would formally declare Chiamaka missing and commence investigations to establish her whereabouts.
